section_summary: This section records maritime incidents involving Japanese and American vessels from January 1940 to March 1941. It covers the sinking of the Sumei Maru, the rescue and return of the Dai Ichi Saiho Maru’s crew, and the grounding of the City of Joliet. Most pages concern the collision between the S.S. Michigan and the Japanese schooner Koshi Maru, including testimony, radio messages, and a later lawsuit; the section also documents the rescue of the Nankai Maru’s crew.

subfiles.title: Sinking of the Sumei Maru
subfiles.about: Reports that a mine sank a Japanese transport near Hankow.
subfiles.summary: A mine sank the Sumei Maru near White Tiger Hill; most aboard survived, and the mine’s origin was uncertain.

subfiles.title: Request for Penguin visit to Saipan
subfiles.about: Seeks permission for the U.S.S. Penguin to deliver a wrecked fishing boat’s crew to Saipan.
subfiles.summary: The Embassy is asked to secure immediate permission for the Penguin’s visit.

subfiles.title: Telephone request concerning the Penguin
subfiles.about: Records Commander Struble’s request for a telegram about returning the Dai Ichi Saiho Maru’s crew.
subfiles.summary: Struble asks State to seek permission for the Penguin to visit Saipan.

subfiles.title: Japanese alternatives for crew transfer
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s proposed arrangements for receiving the wrecked fishing boat’s crew.
subfiles.summary: Japan proposes collecting the crew at Guam or receiving them at Rota after transport by the Penguin.

subfiles.title: Navy acceptance of Rota proposal
subfiles.about: Records the Navy Department’s acceptance of the proposed transfer at Rota.
subfiles.summary: Commander Struble reports Navy approval and requests a reply to Tokyo.

subfiles.title: Approval of Penguin visit to Rota
subfiles.about: Accepts delivery at Rota and asks when the Penguin can make the visit.
subfiles.summary: State accepts the Rota plan and requests the earliest possible date.

subfiles.title: Tokyo telegram forwarded to Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards the Embassy’s report on Japan’s response to the Saipan request.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Tokyo’s January 17 telegram for the Navy.

subfiles.title: Storm damage at Rota pier
subfiles.about: Reports that storm damage complicates the planned survivor transfer at Rota.
subfiles.summary: Rota’s pier is unusable; Japan is arranging details and expects the Penguin can depart January 20.

subfiles.title: Rota update forwarded to Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards Tokyo’s latest report concerning the U.S.S. Penguin.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the January 19 Embassy telegram.

subfiles.title: Transfer to Saipan Maru off Rota
subfiles.about: Reports Japan’s request for a transfer at sea to the Saipan Maru.
subfiles.summary: Japan requests delivery of the survivors to the Saipan Maru off Rota that afternoon.

subfiles.title: Saipan Maru update forwarded to Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards the Embassy’s report on delivery to the Saipan Maru.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Tokyo’s January 20 telegram on the proposed at-sea transfer.

subfiles.title: Disposition of wrecked vessel’s papers
subfiles.about: Considers how to transfer papers recovered from the Dai Ichi Saiho Maru.
subfiles.summary: Officials favor direct delivery at Saipan and suggest consulting the Navy Judge Advocate General.

subfiles.title: Governor of Guam’s wreck report
subfiles.about: Records a report that the Dai Ichi Saiho Maru wrecked on Guam with all 24 crew safe.
subfiles.summary: The Governor requests arrangements for returning the crew and guidance on the vessel’s recovered papers.

subfiles.title: Embassy despatch on the Saipan request
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Summarizes diplomatic correspondence over returning the Dai Ichi Saiho Maru’s crew.
subfiles.summary: Grew reports the American request to enter Saipan and Japan’s proposal to receive the crew at Guam or Rota; he encloses both notes.

subfiles.title: American request to enter Saipan
subfiles.about: Requests permission for the Penguin to enter Saipan to deliver the shipwrecked crew.
subfiles.summary: Grew asks for an urgent reply to the Saipan entry request.

subfiles.title: Japanese reply on receiving the crew
subfiles.about: Offers to send a vessel to Guam or Rota for the shipwrecked crew.
subfiles.summary: Arita asks which island is more convenient for the transfer.

subfiles.title: Saipan despatch forwarded to Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards Grew’s despatch about permission for the Penguin to visit Saipan.
subfiles.summary: Encloses despatch no. 4455 of January 29.

subfiles.title: City of Joliet stranding cross-reference
subfiles.about: Points to a telegram reporting salvage preparations for the stranded City of Joliet.
subfiles.summary: References a March 29 telegram concerning a salvage boat sent from Kobe.

subfiles.title: Condition and salvage of the City of Joliet
subfiles.about: Reports on the stranded City of Joliet and assistance from Vice Consul Stephan.
subfiles.summary: Two holds are flooded, but the crew is safe and salvage is expected. Stephan intervened after Japanese gendarmes suggested that the master and crew abandon the ship in a fortified zone.

subfiles.title: Japanese appreciation for aid to shipwrecked crew
subfiles.from: Joseph C. Grew, American Embassy, Tokyo
subfiles.about: Forwards Japan’s thanks for assistance given to the Dai Ichi Saiho Maru’s crew.
subfiles.summary: Grew encloses a translated note of appreciation and reports that Guam authorities received a copy.

subfiles.title: Japanese note of appreciation
subfiles.about: Thanks American authorities for sheltering and transporting the shipwrecked crew.
subfiles.summary: Arita asks that Japan’s gratitude be conveyed to Navy and Guam officials.

subfiles.title: Appreciation despatch forwarded to Navy
subfiles.about: Forwards Japan’s appreciation for aid to the Dai Ichi Saiho Maru’s crew.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Grew’s March 4 despatch and the translated Japanese note.

subfiles.title: Initial Michigan collision allegation
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese claim that the S.S. Michigan sank a fishing boat near Etorofu.
subfiles.summary: Sokobin plans to question the Michigan’s master when the ship reaches Tsingtao.

subfiles.title: Michigan master’s protest and survivor
subfiles.about: Reports the Michigan’s marine protest and discovery of the schooner’s master aboard.
subfiles.summary: The Michigan searched unsuccessfully after the collision. A Japanese survivor appeared aboard four days later; Japanese officials thanked the ship for treating him and gave no indication whether they would sue.

subfiles.title: Consular investigation of Michigan collision
subfiles.about: Reports American and Japanese accounts of the collision and encloses a protest and radio messages.
subfiles.summary: Sokobin describes the Michigan’s account, its search, and the unexpected discovery of schooner master Sadajirō Hōjō aboard. Japanese consular officials identify the lost Koshi Maru, recount Hōjō’s initial statement, and express thanks for his care. No damage action had yet been indicated.

subfiles.title: Certified marine extended protest of the Michigan
subfiles.from: John Grondahl and Michigan crew, before Samuel Sokobin
subfiles.about: Records sworn accounts of the Michigan’s collision with an unidentified schooner.
subfiles.summary: Grondahl, the second mate, and crew members describe the lights, course changes, collision, and prolonged search for the schooner. The formal protest preserves their account and contests responsibility for any resulting loss or damage.

subfiles.title: Michigan broadcast warning
subfiles.about: Warns other ships to watch for a possibly disabled schooner.
subfiles.summary: Broadcasts the collision position and asks vessels to keep lookout.

subfiles.title: Michigan collision report to Kobe
subfiles.about: Reports the schooner collision to the ship’s Kobe office.
subfiles.summary: Gives the collision position and describes searching nearby waters.

subfiles.title: Michigan collision report to Portland
subfiles.about: Reports the collision and search to the ship’s home office.
subfiles.summary: Describes a small schooner, the search, and uncertainty about its damage.

subfiles.title: Michigan search update to Kobe
subfiles.about: Updates the Kobe office on the search for the schooner.
subfiles.summary: Reports no schooner or wreckage found and a course toward Shikotan.

subfiles.title: Michigan search update to Portland
subfiles.about: Updates the home office on the unsuccessful schooner search.
subfiles.summary: Reports no wreckage and a course toward Shikotan.

subfiles.title: Further search report to Portland
subfiles.about: Reports a renewed search before heading toward Shikotan.
subfiles.summary: A second search finds nothing; the ship proceeds toward Shikotan.

subfiles.title: Michigan proceeds to Tsingtao
subfiles.about: Reports the end of the schooner search.
subfiles.summary: After finding nothing, the Michigan proceeds to Tsingtao.

subfiles.title: No sighting near Shikotan
subfiles.about: Reports no sighting near Shikotan and continuation toward Tsingtao.
subfiles.summary: No schooner is seen; the Michigan resumes its voyage.

subfiles.title: Survivor discovered aboard Michigan
subfiles.about: Reports finding a man from the schooner aboard the Michigan.
subfiles.summary: A radiogram identifies the survivor and the schooner from information he supplied.

subfiles.title: Medical needs of Japanese survivor
subfiles.about: Advises that a Japanese survivor with an injured foot is aboard.
subfiles.summary: Requests medical attention when the Michigan arrives at Tsingtao.

subfiles.title: Japanese accounts of Michigan collision
subfiles.about: Forwards translations of Hōjō’s affidavit and disaster report.
subfiles.summary: Sokobin finds the survivor’s account generally straightforward but notes a leading question about responsibility and an unspecified rudder direction. He reports that no damage suit is yet known.

subfiles.title: Affidavit of Sadajirō Hōjō
subfiles.from: Sadajirō Hōjō, questioned by Japanese consular police
subfiles.about: Gives the Koshi Maru master’s detailed account of the collision and his survival.
subfiles.summary: Hōjō describes the schooner’s voyage, crew, collision, and his climb aboard the Michigan. Fearing for his safety, he hid among the lumber for four days before receiving care from the American crew. He discusses the missing crew, responsibility for the collision, and his family; the translation records a certification dated May 14.

subfiles.title: Hōjō’s report of disaster at sea
subfiles.about: Formally reports the Koshi Maru’s sinking and his rescue.
subfiles.summary: Hōjō outlines the voyage, collision, probable sinking, his concealment aboard the Michigan, and the crew’s kindness after he emerged. He fears the other 14 men are lost.

subfiles.title: Second translation of Hōjō affidavit
subfiles.from: Wm. C. Affeld Jr., American Consulate, Kobe
subfiles.about: Sends another translation of the Koshi Maru master’s affidavit for comparison.
subfiles.summary: Affeld forwards a translation prepared by the States Steamship Company’s Japanese translator.

subfiles.title: Alternate translation of Hōjō deposition
subfiles.from: Sadajirō Hōjō, questioned by Japanese consular police
subfiles.about: Provides an alternate English translation of Hōjō’s account of the collision.
subfiles.summary: The deposition recounts the Koshi Maru’s voyage, the collision, Hōjō’s four days hiding aboard the Michigan, and his later treatment. It also records his answers about navigation, the missing crew, legal responsibility, and his family. A Japanese Consul General certified the copy on May 14.

subfiles.title: Japanese thanks for Nankai Maru rescue
subfiles.about: Expresses gratitude for the S.S. Dr. Lykes’s rescue of the Nankai Maru’s crew.
subfiles.summary: The note recounts the motorboat’s storm and drift, rescue by Captain Jahn’s ship, arrival at Honolulu, and return to Japan. It asks that Japan’s thanks be passed to those concerned.

subfiles.title: Japanese thanks forwarded to Maritime Commission
subfiles.about: Forwards Japan’s note thanking the rescuers of the Nankai Maru crew.
subfiles.summary: Encloses the Ambassador’s note and says its contents were communicated to Lykes Brothers.

subfiles.title: Japanese thanks conveyed to Lykes Brothers
subfiles.from: Breckinridge Long, for the Secretary of State
subfiles.about: Conveys Japan’s appreciation for the rescue by the S.S. Dr. Lykes.
subfiles.summary: Long quotes the Japanese Ambassador’s account of the rescue and his thanks to the ship’s captain and crew.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser’s routing suggestion
subfiles.about: Suggests seeking the Justice Department’s views on a legal question.
subfiles.summary: Recommends sending a telegram copy to Justice for any comment it wishes to make.

subfiles.title: Japanese lawsuit over Michigan collision
subfiles.about: Reports a Japanese damages suit and asks about the court’s jurisdiction.
subfiles.summary: The Koshi Maru’s owner has sued States Steamship Company for the vessel and losses associated with the missing crew. The company questions Japanese jurisdiction over a high-seas collision; Sokobin seeks the Department’s view.

subfiles.title: Request for Attorney General’s views
subfiles.about: Seeks comment on Japanese court jurisdiction in the Michigan collision suit.
subfiles.summary: Encloses Sokobin’s radiogram and requests any view on its jurisdiction question.

subfiles.title: Far Eastern Affairs advice on precedent
subfiles.about: Suggests replying to Kobe’s request for a relevant collision precedent.
subfiles.summary: The division recommends telling the consul that State has no useful precedent on record.

subfiles.title: Legal Adviser’s note on precedent
subfiles.about: Considers whether State has a precedent relevant to the Michigan suit.
subfiles.summary: The writer knows of no helpful precedent and questions whether a reply is needed.

subfiles.title: Kobe counsel accepts jurisdiction
subfiles.about: Reports counsel’s revised view of Japanese jurisdiction and request for precedent.
subfiles.summary: Counsel accepts Kobe District Court jurisdiction but seeks a comparable high-seas collision case.

subfiles.title: No precedent available
subfiles.about: Replies to the request for a precedent in the Michigan proceedings.
subfiles.summary: State reports that it has no precedent likely to assist the company.

subfiles.title: Justice Department response on jurisdiction
subfiles.from: Francis M. Shea, for the Attorney General
subfiles.about: Responds to State’s request for comment on the Japanese litigation.
subfiles.summary: Justice offers no view; the private parties can raise jurisdiction before the Japanese courts.

subfiles.title: Commerce request for collision despatches
subfiles.about: Requests copies of Tsingtao despatches for a federal investigation of the Michigan collision.
subfiles.summary: Commerce seeks despatches 357 and 366 for the Bureau of Marine Inspection and Navigation.
